description: The finite-difference block Jacobian does not robustly converge the buoyancy-coupled mass+energy system at the high permeability (k~1.4e-9) that supercritical Rayleigh numbers need (residual stalls ~4e-2). Add an analytic block Jacobian and/or adaptive timestepping so the two #[ignore]d HRL onset tests (buoyancy_onset_across_critical_rayleigh, heated_from_above_stays_stable) in src/thermal_convection pass. Split from op-v6s.15.6.
title: Robust convecting-regime solve for thermal_convection (HRL onset)

description:
Remaining scope from op-dt3.26, which covered (p,s), the two-phase (T,p,x) family, alpha_v/kappa_t on both (T,p) and (p,h), and the TampinesSteamTableCV constructors, but deliberately left (h,s) uncovered rather than half-gate it.

STILL UNCOVERED, all panic-only:
  hs_flash_eqm::t_hs_eqm, p_hs_eqm, v_hs_eqm, x_hs_eqm, cp_hs_eqm, w_hs_eqm,
  kappa_hs_eqm, mu_hs_eqm, lambda_hs_eqm, tpvx_hs_flash_eqm, hs_flash_region,
  find_pressure_from_hs_region_4
  plus TampinesSteamTableCV::new_from_hs, which resolves pressure via p_hs_eqm
  and so inherits the whole surface.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN op-dt3.26. Unlike (p,h) and (p,s), the (h,s) panic surface is not two bound checks. Traced 2026-08-11, there are 26 distinct panic!/todo!/unimplemented! sites:

  - hs_flash_eqm/mod.rs:389,392 - global entropy band [-0.00858, 11.92] kJ/(kg K)
  - nine entropy-band sub-routers (hs_region_low_entropy_region_1_and_4 through
    hs_region_high_entropy_region_2a_only), lines 511,516,538,542,584,588,611,615,
    636,640,679,683,756,760,794,804,816,843,847,884,889,921,926 - each panics on an
    enthalpy bound computed by h_ps_eqm(p_hi, s) / h_ps_eqm(p_lo, s), i.e. by a
    (p,s) flash that itself panics
  - additional_temperature_check_for_1073_15_k_isotherm at 958,961,971,980 - two
    entropy bounds plus a resolved-temperature check that runs p_hs_2a/2b then
    t_ph_eqm (so it also inherits the (p,h) panic surface)
  - find_pressure_from_hs_region_4:1033 - 'Solution not bracketed by pressure
    bounds', a BISECTION FAILURE, not an envelope violation
  - mod.rs:365 unimplemented!('Region 5 does not have (h,s) flashing') - believed
    unreachable, no sub-router returns Region5; needs confirming, not assuming
  - validity_range.rs:50 todo!() in hs_is_below_isobar_p_100_mpa_in_region1 -
    reachable only if that fn is called with h <= 1670.9 kJ/kg and s <= 3.778
    kJ/(kg K); currently no caller inside the crate, but it is pub

A faithful gate therefore has to MIRROR the entropy-band dispatch, not add a bounds check: pick the same band, compute the same enthalpy bounds (running check_ps_envelope first so the h_ps_eqm calls are themselves safe), mirror the 1073.15 K isotherm check (with check_ph_envelope before its t_ph_eqm), and then gate the post-routing calls too, since tpvx_hs_flash_eqm goes on to call v_ps_eqm(p_resolved, s) and x_ph_flash(p_resolved, h) with a pressure that comes out of a backward equation.

The bisection panic at :1033 cannot be gated by any input bounds check. Recommend find_pressure_from_hs_region_4 be changed to return Result (a separate, non-additive change needing maintainer sign-off), or the checked (h,s) facade be documented as covering the envelope panics only - which by the op-dt3.26 no-half-gating rule means it should not ship until that is resolved.

REQUIRED PATTERN (unchanged from op-t647/op-dt3.26): no catch_unwind ever; NaN rejected explicitly; typed errors; uom on the public surface; doc comments stating physical quantity, valid range and units; a panic-site-to-gate table in the module doc; and a sweep of the accepted set proving zero leaked panics before the gate is called complete.
title: tampines-steam-tables: bounds-checked facade for the (h,s) flash family

description: O(n^3) -> O(n) in the hottest loop of the only fidelity band that currently runs in real time. thomas_solve already exists in the crate. Pair with the criterion harness bead so the improvement is measured, not asserted.
title: tuas: replace the dense LU on the tridiagonal conductance matrix with thomas_solve

description:
Foundation for the rest of `op-yvj.4`. Everything else depends on this.

Deliver the dispatch layer itself, no kernels:

- `ComputeBackend { Serial, CpuMulti, Gpu }` — enum dispatch, per the workspace
  Rust design rules (no `dyn`, no `Box`, no lifetime params). Shared GPU device
  / queue state held as `Arc<T>`.
- A **backend-selection policy** that is explicit and documented: what problem
  size or batch count makes a GPU dispatch worth the host-device transfer, and
  what happens below it (fall back to `CpuMulti`, then `Serial`). Auto-select
  must be a named function a reader can find, not scattered `if n > 1024`.
- **Cargo features**: `gpu` (wgpu) and `parallel` (rayon), both **off by
  default** so the default build stays Android-clean and dependency-light.
- **Android/Termux gating** (hard rule, epic `op-zfr`): wgpu declared only
  under `[target.'cfg(not(target_os = "android"))'.dependencies]`; every
  GPU-touching test/bench carries `#![cfg(not(target_os = "android"))]` and
  every GPU-touching example gets an Android stub `main`. Acceptance is
  `cargo check -p outram-foam-basic-lib --all-targets --target
  aarch64-linux-android` clean, with a native Termux build as the
  authoritative check.
- **Graceful absence of a GPU**: no adapter, no panic — log once and fall back.
- Module-level `//!` doc explaining what belongs in the backend module and what
  does not (human-interface-layer rule).

Look at how `njoy-outram-park-fork` and `outram-mc-libs` (`op-u6s.3`) already
gate their wgpu paths and reuse that shape rather than inventing a third one.
If the shape generalises, note whether it should eventually live in one place
instead of three.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: ComputeBackend enum (Serial/CpuMulti/Gpu) + dispatch policy + feature/Android gating
